description: Replace the per-matrix tridiagonal path with a cached custom extension around CUDA batched symmetric eigensolvers: prioritize portable cusolverDnSsyevjBatched, explore dynamically gated XsyevBatched, and dispatch by size while tuning Jacobi sweeps, tolerance, sorting, workspace reuse, and row/column-major output views.
Generic XsyevBatched extension compiled, but the leaderboard static gate rejected explicit CUDA stream API usage before runtime validation.
Generic cuSOLVER XsyevBatched on every size passed all 39 validation cases and scored 50717.546 us geomean versus the 56277.006 us baseline (1.110x).

Forced XsyevBatched ALG_1 passed validation and scored 52665.977 us; n=32 slowed from 126.285 to 210.174 us while larger sizes were approximately unchanged, confirming the default Blackwell small-size switch is valuable.

Legacy syevjBatched at n<=352 (tol 1e-5, 30 sweeps, sorted) passed validation and scored 57635.984 us. It improved n=32 from 126.285 to 119.764 us but regressed n=176 from 3114.937 to 11735.316 us and n=352 from 19612.246 to 29066.686 us.

Dispatched only n=32 to syevjBatched at tol 2e-4/max 10, with XsyevBatched elsewhere. Validation passed (n=32 scaled eigen residual 69.9) and geomean improved to 50300.951 us; nsys shows the Jacobi kernel at 102.34 us plus 2.32 us bookkeeping.

Jacobi tolerance 4e-4 passed test validation but failed the benchmark's obligatory correctness check at n=32 (scaled eigen residual 202 versus 200 allowed), bracketing the tolerance ceiling below 4e-4.

Jacobi tolerance 3e-4 with max 10 sweeps passed both test and benchmark correctness, scoring 50247.549 us. The n=32 shape improved to 111.807 us from 113.937 us at 2e-4; this is the best measured full-set score so far.
Jacobi tolerance 3.5e-4/max 10 passed benchmark correctness and measured 50192.861 us geomean, with n=32 at 111.384 us. This marginally improved the run's best while bracketing failure at 4e-4.

Reduced the n=32 Jacobi cap from 10 to 7 sweeps at tol 3.5e-4. Validation residuals were identical and n=32 measured 111.271 us, indicating convergence before the cap; full geomean 50217.626 us differed from trial 8 within noise.
Capping Jacobi at five sweeps failed n=32 validation (scaled eigen residual 404 versus 200), while seven sweeps had converged; the useful sweep boundary is therefore six or seven.

Six Jacobi sweeps at tol 3.5e-4 passed validation and benchmark, while five failed; n=32 remained 111.389 us, showing six is the minimum passing cap without changing converged runtime. Full geomean measured 50144.241 us (1.122x baseline).

Size-gated PyTorch fallbacks at n=176/352/2048 scored 50522.869 us. Each was slower than XsyevBatched: 3148.691 vs 3080.975 us, 20775.749 vs 19413.511 us, and 183967.113 vs 182331.553 us respectively, so Xsyev remains preferred above n=32.

Restored XsyevBatched for every n>32 and allocated its cached host workspace as pinned memory. Validation passed; 50201.278 us geomean was within noise of the 50144.241 us pageable-workspace result, with no consistent per-shape gain.

Using the column-major upper triangle in both solvers passed validation but regressed geomean to 51674.193 us; n=512/1024 cases slowed roughly 3.5-5%. The n=2048 case improved from recent lower-triangle 182.3-182.5 ms to 180.855 ms, motivating a size-gated triangle path.

Lower triangle through n=1024 with upper at n>=2048 passed validation and scored 50097.009 us, the best measured result (1.123x baseline). n=2048 improved to 180369.997 us; nsys shows upper SYMV kernels dominate 33.9% of captured GPU time.

Combined upper-triangle n>=2048 with forced XsyevBatched ALG_1. Validation passed; n=2048 measured 180480.851 us versus 180369.997 us with default selection, and full geomean 50138.598 us was within noise but not better.

Extended six-sweep Jacobi (tol 3.5e-4) through n=352. Validation passed, but n=176 was 10223.316 us versus ~3083 us for Xsyev; n=352 improved over strict Jacobi to 22399.183 us yet remained slower than ~19431 us Xsyev. Full geomean 55586.891 us.
Five-sweep Jacobi at n=352 failed validation with scaled eigen residual 608 versus 200; six sweeps pass but measure 22.4 ms versus ~19.4 ms for Xsyev, bracketing the viable crossover.

Replaced ATen clone with empty_like plus direct default-queue device copy. Validation passed; n=32 remained 111.137 us and full geomean 50168.127 us showed no consistent improvement over the 50097.009 us clone path.

Removed device guards and task-contract assertions while restoring Tensor::clone. Validation passed; n=32 remained 111.311 us and full geomean was 50266.018 us, so host checks were not material. nsys reports 99.75 us Jacobi plus 2.32 us sort bookkeeping.

Restored measured-best solver dispatch: legacy Jacobi only at n=32 (tol 3.5e-4, 6 sweeps), generic Xsyev elsewhere, upper triangle at n>=2048; final clean rerun passed and SHA-matched n2048 profile captured.

Built and measured 21 variants. Best/final source scored 50097.009 us (1.123x baseline): Jacobi only at n=32 with tolerance 3.5e-4 and six sweeps, Xsyev elsewhere, upper triangle at n>=2048. Final SHA d263904233cf829e16b862d5c00a5b81edf7f9c0 passes all 39 validation cases and clean-reran at 50212.374 us with a SHA-matched n2048 profile. Keep exploring: a fused sorted n32 eigenpair path could remove the measured ~2.3 us sorting stage; large-Xsyev batch chunk sizes may improve workspace/occupancy; n2048 upper-path chunking and algorithm/workspace combinations remain open; output-buffer pooling may remove allocator cost if lifecycle correctness can be preserved.

Replace the per-matrix tridiagonal path with a cached custom extension around CUDA batched symmetric eigensolvers: prioritize portable cusolverDnSsyevjBatched, explore dynamically gated XsyevBatched, and dispatch by size while tuning Jacobi sweeps, tolerance, sorting, workspace reuse, and row/column-major output views.

Enabled CUSOLVER_FP32_EMULATED_BF16X9_MATH on the generic Xsyev handle. All 39 tests passed; geomean was 50078.190 us. n=1024 cases improved roughly 0.4-0.7% versus the final fallback rerun while n=512 was essentially unchanged. nsys confirms six Blackwell BF16x9 tensor-op GEMMs, but SYMV/GEMV remain 61% of n=1024 kernel time.

Forced CUDA_EMULATION_STRATEGY_EAGER with BF16x9 solver math. All validation cases passed, but geomean regressed to 50858.219 us because n=2048 rose to 225059.786 us from 180638.080 us under the default performant strategy; n=512/1024 were nearly unchanged.

Restored default BF16x9 strategy and split benchmark-scale Xsyev batches in half while reusing one chunk workspace. Validation passed; geomean regressed to 61065.530 us. Relative to one packed call, n=512 rose about 11%, n=1024 about 42%, and n=2048 about 80%, with 174721.975/152226.827/324247.864 us representative timings.

Restored full-batch BF16x9 Xsyev and pooled output slots only when tensor/storage ownership proved no live external outputs. All tests passed, including benchmark retained-output rechecks. Geomean was 50167.192 us; n=2048 measured 182350.210 us, so safe allocation reuse did not improve the solve-dominated path. SHA-matched n2048 nsys captured.

Restored clone outputs and replaced Jacobi's built-in ordering with a fused CUB warp sort plus shared-memory eigenvector permutation. All tests passed. n=32 improved from about 111.2 to 107.369 us and full geomean reached 50053.018 us. nsys shows unsorted Jacobi fell from 99.75 to 91.47 us; the fused postprocess costs 2.77 us, while the 2.31 us cuSOLVER music kernel remains.

Reduced fused n=32 ordering launch from 256 to 128 threads. Validation passed; n=32 was unchanged within noise at 107.469 us, while a stable n=2048 sample (180380.814 us) yielded a new full geomean low of 49929.894 us.

Completed the fused ordering block-size sweep at 64 threads. Validation passed; n=32 rose to 108.461 us versus 107.469/107.369 us at 128/256 threads, and full geomean was 50044.930 us with a noisy 182754.501 us n=2048 sample.

Enabled CUSOLVER_ALLOW_NON_DETERMINISTIC_RESULTS on the generic BF16x9 Xsyev handle while leaving the 64-thread ordering endpoint unchanged. Validation passed; geomean was 49930.277 us, n=2048 was 180056.564 us (about 0.18% below the deterministic 128-thread run), and other large groups were effectively unchanged.

Combined the 128-thread fused n=32 ordering kernel with non-deterministic BF16x9 Xsyev scheduling. Validation passed; n=32 reached 107.296 us, n=2048 was 180939.373 us, and geomean was 49980.666 us. The checkpoint nsys profile shows the same dominant upper-SYMV/GEMV structure as deterministic execution.

Raised the six-sweep n=32 Jacobi tolerance from 3.5e-4 to 3.75e-4. The 39 test cases passed, but benchmark seed 43214 failed its recheck on matrix 10 with scaled eigen residual 202 versus the limit 200, matching the previously observed 4e-4 boundary failure.

Tested six-sweep Jacobi tolerance 3.6e-4 after 3.75e-4 failed. The test suite passed, but benchmark seed 43214 again failed on matrix 10 with the identical scaled eigen residual 202 versus 200, placing the discrete convergence transition between 3.5e-4 and 3.6e-4.

Bisected the six-sweep Jacobi tolerance at 3.55e-4. Tests passed, but benchmark seed 43214 again produced the discrete matrix-10 scaled eigen residual 202 versus 200. The measured safe endpoint remains 3.5e-4.

Forced CUSOLVER_ALG_1 only at n>=2048 on the deterministic BF16x9 candidate. Validation passed and geomean was 49928.952 us, statistically tied with the prior best; n=2048 measured 180566.401 us versus 180380.814 us under default algorithm selection.

Extended BF16x9 CUSOLVER_ALG_1 from n>=2048 to n>=1024. Validation passed and geomean was 49931.666 us; all n=1024 cases remained within sub-percent noise of default selection. A SHA-matched n=1024 nsys checkpoint was captured for the algorithm/workspace comparison.

Restored the simplest measured-best source: default Xsyev algorithm selection with BF16x9 math, full batches, lower triangle through n=1024 and upper at n=2048, plus 128-thread fused n=32 eigenpair ordering. All 39 tests passed. Final clean geomean was 49645.576 us (1.134x baseline), with n=32 107.306 us and n=2048 172985.875 us; SHA-matched n=2048 nsys captured.

Continuation measured 15 additional trials. Final/best source e8704bc6a8db3512e2488d34d2a57fec1e514a5e passes all 39 tests and scored 49645.576 us (1.134x baseline; prior accepted source was 50097.009 us). Blackwell BF16x9 math exposed tensor-op GEMMs but SYMV/GEMV remain dominant; eager emulation regressed n=2048 to 225 ms. Half-batch chunks regressed n=512/1024/2048 by about 11/42/80%, and ownership-safe output pooling was neutral. Disabling Jacobi ordering plus one fused CUB eigenpair reorder cut n=32 from about 111.2 to 107.3 us; 128/256 threads beat 64. Tolerances 3.55e-4 and above failed benchmark residual 202 versus 200, so 3.5e-4 remains accepted. Forced ALG_1 at n=1024/2048 and non-deterministic scheduling were sub-percent neutral. Keep exploring: replace dominant Xsyev SYMV/GEMV phases with a tensor-core reduction/eigensolver design; fuse or eliminate the remaining 2.3 us syevj music bookkeeping and 2.8 us n=32 reorder; test solver math emulation controls beyond eager/default; and investigate concurrent independent large-matrix solves with lifecycle-safe handle/workspace ownership.

Replace the per-matrix tridiagonal path with a cached custom extension around CUDA batched symmetric eigensolvers: prioritize portable cusolverDnSsyevjBatched, explore dynamically gated XsyevBatched, and dispatch by size while tuning Jacobi sweeps, tolerance, sorting, workspace reuse, and row/column-major output views.

Added a CUDART_VERSION>=13030 guard around BF16x9 math and force-disabled that branch locally to compile the exact CUDA-13.0 fallback without either missing identifier. Build and all 39 tests passed; default-math geomean was 49964.942 us (1.126x baseline), with fused n=32 ordering retained at 107.298 us.
CUDA-version guarded BF16x9 math: CUDA 13.3 enables tensor-core emulation while CUDA 13.0 compiles default math; all 39 validation cases pass
CUDA 13.3 tensor-core math dispatch only for n>=1024, restoring default Xsyev math for smaller matrices; CUDA 13.0 guard preserved; all 39 tests pass
CUDA 13.3 BF16x9 tensor-core math for n>=512 and default math below; CUDA 13.0 fallback preserved; all 39 tests pass

Portable CUDA compatibility is implemented and measured. Commit 23f6c4c48 forced the CUDA-13.0 fallback branch to compile and passed all 39 tests at 49964.942 us; ac66f6ead enabled the CUDA-version-guarded CUDA-13.3 BF16x9 path; final d05f2986e keeps that guard and dispatches BF16x9 for n>=512, passes kernelguard/all 39 tests, and measures 49863.230 us. Nsys trial 40 confirms n512 BF16x9 tensor-op kernels but only 0.2% of GPU time plus about 0.4% patching, while SYMV/GEMV/tridiagonal stages dominate. Explicit concurrent solves are not leaderboard-legal because validation rejects any source containing stream. Remaining useful work is fleet combination/remote CUDA-13.0 submission and comparison against other briefs; do not submit or combine the unguarded e8704bc6 source. If continuing this branch, focus on legal Xsyev algorithm/triangle dispatch or custom non-streamed reductions, not additional BF16 threshold tuning.
